summary: A good-value Bangkok dish rather than a single attraction: for a reliable tom yum pork noodle stop, try Rung Rueang Pork Noodles on Sukhumvit Soi 26. Its dry tom yum version is a useful way to experience the sour, chilli-forward seasoning without committing to a soup bowl.
whyGo: This everyday noodle-shop meal gives a direct taste of Bangkok's hot-sour noodle style, with a choice of noodles and pork toppings.
Time Out recommends dry tom yum pork noodles and crispy fish skin at Rung Rueang; it reports a current listed price of ฿60–80.
bestFor: A quick, inexpensive lunch near Phrom Phong.
Travellers comfortable with casual seating and pork-based menus.
skipIf: You need a confirmed vegetarian, vegan, halal or allergy-safe meal; those options and cross-contact practices were not verified.
You want dinner: the recommended shop is listed as closing at 5pm.
duration: Allow about 30–60 minutes for the meal and any queue (planning estimate; queue length varies).
cost: Time Out lists ฿60–80 for the featured shop (checked October 2026); allow extra for drinks or sides. Prices may change before December.
hours: Rung Rueang at 10/3 Sukhumvit Soi 26 is listed daily 8am–5pm by Time Out and the Tourism Authority of Thailand's Japanese-language site. Reconfirm close to travel, especially around public holidays.
bestTime: Go after opening or outside the lunch rush. The Tourism Authority of Thailand warns that queues build around lunchtime; exact December wait times are unknown.
gettingThere: Take the BTS Sukhumvit Line to Phrom Phong, then walk about five minutes into Soi Sukhumvit 26. Rung Rueang's adjacent, similarly named shops can be confusing: confirm the 10/3 address and sign if following Time Out's recommendation.
booking: No advance booking is needed for a casual noodle meal; Michelin says the listed shop handles booking enquiries directly. No reliable online reservation channel was confirmed. Check current service before making a special trip.
accessibility: The open-air shophouse setting is described by Michelin, but step-free access, accessible toilets, seating suitability and queue accommodations are not documented in the sources. Contact the shop directly if these are essential.
practicalTips: Ask for tom yum noodles; choose soup or dry style and a noodle type. The dry version is Time Out's highlighted order.
Add fried fish skin for crunch if desired; ask staff about ingredients if you have dietary restrictions.
Bring cash: Michelin lists the shop as cash only.
This is a pork-noodle specialist, not a seafood tom yum bowl; don't assume a particular topping is available without asking.
decemberNotes: No December 2026 event or holiday schedule was published in the sources checked. The currently listed daily hours are not a guarantee for Christmas, New Year or other holiday dates; check the shop's latest notice before travelling. Bangkok can still be hot, so choose indoor/covered seating if available.
uncertainties: Opening hours and ฿60–80 price are current listings, not December 2026 guarantees.
There are two adjacent Rung Rueang businesses; listings vary between 10/3 and 21/2 Sukhumvit Soi 26, so verify which shop you intend to visit.
The sources do not establish specific allergy handling, dietary alternatives, step-free access or holiday closures.
